summary.one_line: Quilting is a large, stable, older and well-off hobby audience that pays for patterns, planners and design tools; quilt calculators are free everywhere, so QPK's calculators are a traffic engine and the money is in planners, patterns and the KDP book.

go_hold.subject: Quilt Plan Kit $8 planner and offer ladder
go_hold.rationale: Strongest evidence of the three: a measured audience (9-11 million active consumers, 2025 survey), a $4.5B industry estimate, and many paid planners at $5-$19 plus patterns at about $5-$20. QPK also has the only live channel (Pinterest).
go_hold.falsifying_test: If checkout is live and QPK gets 300+ sessions to the planner page in 60 days with zero sales, revisit price and offer. Owner-adjustable rule, not a forecast.

key_findings.statement: The 2025 Quilter's Survey (30,000+ responses) reports 9-11 million active quilting consumers, stable for ten years, with 18% of respondents new to quilting.
The typical respondent is a woman in her 60s, retired, household income $75K+, about 10 years quilting, starting 11 and finishing 9 projects a year.
Industry revenue is estimated at $4.50B (2025) rising to $4.58B (2027 estimate).
In 2014, 'dedicated' quilters (12.2% of quilting households) spent an average $3,296 a year and made up 60.4% of industry spending.
Paid quilt planners sell at $5, $6, $15 and $19; the $19 one bundles a pattern and videos.
Quilt calculators are free from apps (QuiltingCalc, 4.3 stars from 147 ratings), retailers (about 30 tools at My Favorite Quilt Store) and indie sites.
64% of supply purchases happen in local quilt shops, and online buying is declining after the pandemic.
